newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM denies cabinet reshuffle planned.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM denies cabinet reshuffle planned.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Tuesday he has no plans to reshuffle his present cabinet, the national Bernama news agency reported.
There was no problem with the present cabinet line-up, he was quoted as telling a news conference in Kota Kinabalu, capital of the east Malaysian Sabah state.
"I am not planning any (reshuffle). Why should I plan any? I have no problem (with the present cabinet)," Bernama quoted him as saying.
The Chinese-language Sin Chew Jit Poh daily reported on Saturday that at least three ministers would be dropped from the cabinet.

The story, picked up by the Sunday Times in neighbouring Singapore, said Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim was likely to lose his finance ministry job to International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz.
The rumours dominated talk in financial markets on Tuesday and influenced movements of the ringgit, but analysts said that the effect was still minimal.

"I think by now Malaysians have accepted that Mahathir knows what he is doing," said an economist with a local stockbroking firm. "If he wants to reshuffle the cabinet, it will be seen as a move to strengthen the government."
"I don't think markets are going to be adversely affected by all these, as politically the country is strong and all fundamentals are good," he added.
The story had said Anwar could be made minister of rural development, a job perceived in political circles as less demanding and less important.

"I don't think Mahathir would want to do this as it doesn't augur well with his plans to have Anwar as his successor if he's going to move him to a less-important ministry," said another economist with a foreign brokerage in Singapore.
Earlier on Tuesday, Anwar dismissed the reshuffling reports as speculation. "The speculation has been there for days, weeks, months, years," he said.
"(Reshuffle) is the sole prerogative of the prime minister and I think the media has taken it up from time to time...every other week it will surface," he said.
The ringgit was lower on Monday morning as the speculation spread, while share prices on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange closed firm on Monday.
"I think the (stock) market should remain bullish and not entertain rumours and speculation," said Anwar.
